question: Which of the following structures stores carbohydrates?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Amyloplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amyloplasts** are a type of plastid found in plant cells.
 
• They are responsible for the **synthesis and storage of starch granules**, which are carbohydrates.
 
• **Amyloplasts** are non-pigmented and do not participate in photosynthesis like chloroplasts.
 
• These structures are primarily found in storage tissues of plants, such as **roots, tubers, and seeds**.
 
• The starch stored in amyloplasts serves as an **energy reserve** for the plant.
 
• Amyloplasts play a key role in the process of **gravity sensing** in plants, as they settle in response to gravitational forces.
 
• They convert glucose into starch through a process of **enzymatic activity** and store it in the form of granules.
 
• Examples of plants where amyloplasts are commonly found include **potatoes, wheat, rice, and maize.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aleuroplast**__

 __
 
• **Aleuroplasts** are specialized plastids that store proteins instead of carbohydrates.
 
• They are typically found in **seeds** and are involved in protein synthesis and storage for germination and growth.
 
• Aleuroplasts play an essential role in nourishing the plant embryo during seed development.
 
 
 
• **Elaioplast**__
 __
 
• **Elaioplasts** are a type of plastid that stores lipids or oils.
 
• These plastids are present in tissues where **energy-rich lipids** are required, such as seeds.
 
• They are associated with the synthesis and storage of **fatty acids**.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast**__
 
 
• **Chloroplasts** are plastids responsible for **photosynthesis** in plant cells.
 
• They contain the green pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures light energy for synthesizing glucose.
 
• Chloroplasts are found in **green tissues** of plants, such as leaves and stems.
 
• Unlike amyloplasts, chloroplasts do not store carbohydrates; they produce them during photosynthesis.
